title: Australian gas project enters home stretch as developments in Mexico and US Gulf make new inroads
summary: Woodside’s Scarborough, Trion, and Louisiana LNG projects have hit new milestones, with the finish line in sight for the first one.
fact_excerpt:
The operator emphasizes that well clean-up results are in line with reservoir and well performance expectations. The company completed all mechanical runs of Pluto Train 2 compressors, and, subsequent to the period, Scarborough gas was introduced to the warm end (gas pre-treatment) of the LNG train.

Activities in the cold end continue to progress, which will enable the start of gas liquefaction. Following the Pluto Train 1 planned major maintenance campaign in Q2, modifications to Pluto Train 1, which will allow processing of Scarborough gas, continued. The final module arrived on-site with activities focused on module hook-up and integration. The first LNG cargo is on track for Q4 2026.

“We delivered quarterly production of 46.2 million barrels of oil equivalent, up 12% from the previous quarter following the successful completion of the Pluto LNG turnaround in the second quarter and the NWS turnaround in the third quarter.”

The Louisiana LNG project remains on budget and was 32% complete at the end of the quarter, as LNG terminal construction advanced across marine, site works, and LNG tanks, with LNG Tank 1 wall concrete reaching 50% completion.

Currently, ongoing engagement with high-quality counterparties for equity participation and LNG offtake continues. The project is targeting the first LNG in 2029. The Australian energy giant claims that structural steel supply challenges associated with ongoing disruptions in the Middle East continue to be mitigated through alternative logistics routes and fabrication sources.

title: Norway set on tapping into Arctic gas potential: New study to unlock 1988 Barents Sea discovery
summary: Norway is targeting untapped Arctic energy by commissioning a new study to shed more light on the 1988 gas discovery in the Barents Sea.
fact_excerpt:
Decades after being left behind in the frozen depths of the High North, a forgotten 1980s gas find in the Barents Sea is getting a second look. As Europe hungers for new energy sources and low-carbon reserves, Norway is launching a fresh push to unlock the untapped potential of the Arctic, starting with a neglected discovery 200 kilometers north of the Arctic Circle.

The Barents Sea is home to a number of discoveries that could hold vast volumes of gas but remains less explored than other parts of the Norwegian Continental Shelf (NCS), with several discoveries in these waters potentially containing significant volumes of gas, according to the Norwegian Offshore Directorate, which emphasizes that a new study could uncover major opportunities for one of these discoveries.

The gas discovery that this study will aim to gain more insight into is Norselhøgda (the well 7226/11-1 ), which is situated about 200 kilometers north of Hammerfest and was made in 1988. The discovery was production-tested, but the acreage was subsequently relinquished to the authorities.

Several comparable discoveries have been made in the area, which include production license 1313 , located to the north of the Norselhøgda discovery and awarded in APA 2025 . The Gro discovery in the Norwegian Sea is another discovery the Norwegian Offshore Directorate hopes to revive, along with the Linerle discovery in the Norwegian Sea.

title: Eni and Libya’s National Oil Corporation turning on the taps at African gas project
summary: This gas project is set to slash 1.5 million tonnes of annual carbon emissions while unlocking fresh energy supplies for a growing domestic grid.
fact_excerpt:
This gas project is set to slash 1.5 million tonnes of annual carbon emissions while unlocking fresh energy supplies for a growing domestic grid.

A gas project off the coast of Libya, which is operated by Mellitah Oil & Gas Libyan Branch, a consortium formed by National Oil Corporation (NOC) of Libya and Eni North Africa, is anticipated to stop decades of costly flaring in its tracks, capturing hundreds of millions of cubic meters of gas to fuel local power plants and feed European export pipelines.

The recovered gas will be supplied to the domestic market, providing an incremental production of around 700 million standard cubic meters per year, helping meet demand from the power generation sector.

In addition, the project will support additional gas volumes available for export to Europe through the GreenStream pipeline. Saipem finished the lifting operations of the gas recovery module for the BGUP earlier this year.

The pre-commissioning activities were planned for approximately 28 kilometers of already laid subsea pipelines to connect the DP3, DP4, and Sabratha platforms to enable the transportation of the recovered gas to the Mellitah treatment complex.

title: Nordic energy players hit paydirt with new gas and condensate discovery
summary: Vår Energi and Equinor have struck gas and condensate in Norwegian waters, packing up to 5.5 million barrels.
fact_excerpt:
Vår Energi and Equinor have struck gas and condensate in Norwegian waters, packing up to 5.5 million barrels.

Norway’s energy duo, Vår Energi and Equinor, have made a gas and condensate find in a new Norwegian Sea license, uncovering a fresh prospect estimated to hold up to 5.5 million barrels of oil equivalent (boe).

Vår Energi and Equinor have made a gas and condensate discovery in the 6407/5-3 S well, which is known as the Lakris prospect in the Gimsan Basin on the Halten Terrace in the Norwegian Sea.

The water depth at the site is 218 meters. The well, which was not formation-tested, but data and samples were collected, will now be permanently plugged and abandoned.

The well 6407/5-3 S encountered gas and condensate in the upper Tilje Formation in heterolithic reservoir rocks, totalling 54 meters, with moderate to poor reservoir quality. The gas/water contact was not encountered in the well.

title: Completing electrification project at Troll
summary: The partial electrification of Troll B and Troll C has reduced emissions by around 330,000 tonnes of CO₂ per year.
fact_excerpt:
The partial electrification of Troll B and Troll C has reduced emissions by around 330,000 tonnes of CO₂ per year. The Troll field continues to deliver high and stable production of oil and gas to Europe with low emissions.

The Troll licence partnership has informed the Norwegian Ministry of Energy that the Troll West Electrification (TWEL) project will be completed after commissioning the first electric export compressor on Troll C, and without installing the second electric export compressor on Troll C, as originally planned in the 2021 plan for development and operation (PDO).

The decision also helps maintain high and stable gas supplies to Europe at a time when energy security remains important. It is expected to make around 2.3 billion standard cubic metres of additional gas available to the European market in 2027 and 2028. This corresponds to approximately two years of gas consumption for around one million European households.

Troll A became the first platform on the Norwegian continental shelf to receive power from shore in 1996. Troll B and Troll C were partially electrified in 2024. TWEL has reduced emissions from the Troll area by around 330,000 tonnes of CO₂ per year, corresponding to approximately 75% of the emission reductions originally planned in the PDO (440,000 tonnes per year). This makes the project one of the largest emissions reduction measures on the Norwegian continental shelf. Overall, the measures have reduced emissions from the Troll area to approximately the same level as in 1999.

title: Cheniere Announces Substantial Completion of CCL Stage 3 Project, Production and Export of 5,000th LNG Cargo
summary: HOUSTON--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Cheniere Energy, Inc. (“Cheniere” or the “Company”) (NYSE: LNG) today announced the achievement of…
fact_excerpt:
Cheniere celebrated its 5,000 th LNG cargo with the loading of the Yari LNG carrier, which departed Sabine Pass on August 29 th en route to Asia. Since the production of its first LNG cargo in 2016, Cheniere has now supplied more than 340 million tonnes of LNG to markets worldwide, and the Company’s LNG platform has grown to represent over 10% of total global LNG capacity.

Cheniere Energy, Inc. is the leading producer and exporter of LNG in the United States, reliably providing a clean, secure, and affordable solution to the growing global need for natural gas. Cheniere is a full-service LNG provider, with capabilities that include gas procurement and transportation, liquefaction, vessel chartering, and LNG delivery. Cheniere has one of the largest liquefaction platforms in the world, consisting of the Sabine Pass and Corpus Christi liquefaction facilities on the U.S. Gulf Coast, with a total combined production capacity of approximately 56 mtpa of LNG in operation and an additional approximately 5 mtpa of expected production capacity under construction. Cheniere is also pursuing liquefaction expansion opportunities and other projects along the LNG value chain. Cheniere is headquartered in Houston, Texas, and has additional offices in London, Singapore, Beijing, Tokyo, Dubai and Washington, D.C.

For additional information, please refer to the Cheniere website at www.cheniere.com and Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

title: Cheniere Highlights 10 Years of LNG Exports in 2025 Corporate Responsibility Report
summary: HOUSTON--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Cheniere Energy, Inc. (“Cheniere” or the “Company”) (NYSE: LNG) today published its 2025 Corporate…
fact_excerpt:
The report celebrates a defining milestone for Cheniere: 10 years since the first cargo of LNG was exported from its Sabine Pass Liquefaction terminal in Louisiana, a shipment that launched a new energy era for the United States as a major supplier of LNG to the world.

“Nearly 5,000 LNG export cargoes later, we take great pride in the fact that our exports have helped reshape global LNG trade dynamics, providing unprecedented liquidity and flexibility to the market, enabling energy supply to reach customers and markets when and where it is needed most.”

Cheniere Energy, Inc. is the leading producer and exporter of LNG in the United States, reliably providing a clean, secure, and affordable solution to the growing global need for natural gas. Cheniere is a full-service LNG provider, with capabilities that include gas procurement and transportation, liquefaction, vessel chartering, and LNG delivery. Cheniere has one of the largest liquefaction platforms in the world, consisting of the Sabine Pass and Corpus Christi liquefaction facilities on the U.S. Gulf Coast, with a total combined production capacity of approximately 55 mtpa of LNG in operation and an additional over 6 mtpa of expected production capacity under construction or in commissioning, inclusive of estimated debottlenecking opportunities. Cheniere is also pursuing liquefaction expansion opportunities and other projects along the LNG value chain. Cheniere is headquartered in Houston, Texas, and has additional offices in London, Singapore, Beijing, Tokyo, Dubai and Washington, D.C.

title: Cheniere Declares Quarterly Dividend
summary: HOUSTON--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Cheniere Energy, Inc. (“Cheniere”) (NYSE: LNG) today announced that its Board of Directors has declared a…
fact_excerpt:
HOUSTON--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Cheniere Energy, Inc. (“Cheniere”) (NYSE: LNG) today announced that its Board of Directors has declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.555 per common share payable on August 18, 2026 to shareholders of record as of the close of business on August 10, 2026.

Cheniere Energy, Inc. is the leading producer and exporter of liquefied natural gas (“LNG”) in the United States, reliably providing a clean, secure, and affordable solution to the growing global need for natural gas. Cheniere is a full-service LNG provider, with capabilities that include gas procurement and transportation, liquefaction, vessel chartering, and LNG delivery. Cheniere has one of the largest liquefaction platforms in the world, consisting of the Sabine Pass and Corpus Christi liquefaction facilities on the U.S. Gulf Coast, with total production capacity of approximately 55 million tonnes per annum (“mtpa”) of LNG in operation and an additional over 6 mtpa of expected production capacity under construction or in commissioning. Cheniere is also pursuing liquefaction expansion opportunities and other projects along the LNG value chain. Cheniere is headquartered in Houston, Texas, and has additional offices in London, Singapore, Beijing, Tokyo, Dubai and Washington, D.C.

For additional information, please refer to the Cheniere website at www.cheniere.com and Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2026, filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

title: About one-fifth of global liquefied natural gas trade flows through the Strait of Hormuz - U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA)
summary: In 2024, about 20% of global liquefied natural gas (LNG) trade transited the Strait of Hormuz, primarily from Qatar. The strait is a critical route for oil and petroleum products as well. Qatar exported about 9.3 billion cubic feet per day (Bcf/d) of LNG through the Strait of Hormuz in 2024, and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) exported about 0.7 Bcf/d, accounting for nearly all LNG flows from the Persian Gulf through Hormuz. We estimate that 83% of the LNG that moved through the Strait of Hormuz in 2024 went from Persian Gulf countries to Asian markets. China, India, and South Korea were the top destinations for LNG moving through the Strait of Hormuz, accounting for 52% of all Hormuz LNG flows in 2024. In 2024, disruptions to LNG flows through the Bab al-Mandeb Strait, which connects the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden and Arabian Sea, and more U.S. LNG exports to Europe pushed LNG exports from Qatar away from Europe to Asia. Kuwait and the UAE imported LNG that originated outside of the Persian Gulf, including from the United States and West Africa. Bahrain began operating an LNG import terminal in April 2025 and also received cargoes that transited Hormuz from outside of the Persian Gulf, including recent cargoes in April and June that originated from the United States.

summary: Chinese refining giant Sinopec Corp has appointed Zhong Fuliang, vice president of its trading arm Unipec, as the new managing director of the unit, according to a company representative. Coal and natural gas markets were poised on Friday to end 2022 with strong gains after a global energy crisis triggered by the Russia-Ukraine war stoked a sharp upswing in prices, while tighter supplies expected in 2023 could fuel more gains. The chief executive of RWE , Germany's top power producer, warned that gas and electricity prices in the country would remain at least twice as high as they were before the energy crisis despite government countermeasures. Russian President Vladimir Putin said on Friday that Russia had become one of China's leading suppliers of oil and gas, with 13.8 billion cubic metres of gas shipped to China via the Power of Siberia pipeline in the first 11 months of 2022. Asian spot liquefied natural gas (LNG) prices slid for a second consecutive week, dragged down by healthy inventory levels in both Asia and Europe amid a relatively mild winter, while also recording an annual decline. Japanese insurers are expected to maintain marine war insurance, which covers the sinking and requisition of ships due to war in Russian waters for at least three months for liquefied natural gas (LNG) vessels, industry sources said on Friday. title: OGDCL finds oil, gas in Pakistan's Sindh province Canada’s Criterium buys stake in Bulu PSC in Indonesia for $1.6mn Malaysia records 10 hydrocarbon discoveries in 2022 Mediterranean Gas says non-binding interest for planned FSRU topped capacity Indonesia, BP sign 20-yr contract extension for LNG operations in Papua Eni's Vaar Energi makes Arctic gas discovery Indonesia aims to export natural gas to Vietnam in 2026 Santos extends exclusivity period for PNG LNG sell down Hungary government raises the capital of state-owned energy company Turkey accuses Cyprus of increasing tension in east Med over gas exploration U.S. Northeast/Texas power and natgas prices soar on extreme cold Freeport LNG delays restart to second half of January
summary: Kot Nawab-1 was spudded in June this year. The Bulu production sharing contract contains the Lengo gas field. Eight oil and gas discoveries were made off the coast of Sarawak, and one each off the coast of Sabah and Peninsular Malaysia. Greece-based Mediterranean Gas has received non-binding interest from domestic and foreign companies which exceeded the capacity of its planned floating gas storage and regasification (FSRU) unit in central Greece, it said on Thursday. Indonesia has extended by 20 years a production sharing contract (PSC) with BP and its partners for Berau, Muturi, and Wiriagar working areas in West Papua, government officials and the company said on Friday. Norway's Vaar Energi, majority owned by Italy's Eni, said on Friday it had made a gas discovery near the Goliat field in the Arctic Barents Sea, supporting the group's long-term plans to expand in the area. Indonesia aims to export natural gas to Vietnam starting 2026 from the Tuna offshore block located near the Indonesian and Vietnamese maritime border, the country's energy minister said on Friday. Santos had in September received a binding conditional offer from Kumul to acquire a 5% interest in PNG LNG for an asset value of $1.4bn. The government of Hungary decided to raise the capital of state-owned energy company MVM Zrt by 41 billion forint ($108.79 million) to 849.4 billion forints, the company said on Friday in a statement on the stock exchange's website. Turkey on Friday accused Cyprus of increasing tension in the Eastern Mediterranean after a consortium of Italian and French energy companies found more natural gas off the island earlier this week. Some natural gas prices hitting multi-year highs as cold, storms blanket most of the nation. Restart has been delayed several times since June explosion and fire. [Image credit: Freeport LNG]

summary: In this latest OIES podcast James Henderson talks to Mike Fulwood, Jack Sharples and Jonathan Stern about the continuing impact of the Russia-Ukraine war on gas markets. Ukrainians are currently scrambling to find enough gas and electricity for the winter heating season following an unprecedented series of Russian attacks on the country’s energy infrastructure. Tamboran will use the fund for an acquisition of an interest in and operatorship of natural gas assets in the Beetaloo sub-basin. Australia on Tuesday appointed former Victoria state premier Steve Bracks as its special representative for the Greater Sunrise gas project in East Timor as both countries look to break a stalemate over how to develop the gas fields. China's inadvertent support for global liquefied natural gas (LNG) markets is likely drawing to a close, as the world's second-biggest buyer of the fuel cuts back on re-selling unneeded cargoes. Output at the project has plummeted since the war in Ukraine began. [image credit: Exxon Neftegaz]. Portugal's oil and gas company Galp Energia said on Monday it may face additional sourcing disruptions after Nigeria LNG declared force majeure due to a widespread flooding. The European Commission is set to propose another set of emergency measures on Tuesday to tackle high energy prices, but draft proposals suggest they will not include an immediate cap on gas prices as EU countries remain split over the idea The Nord Stream 1 and Yamal-Europe pipelines are both out of action, and there is a risk that transit through Ukraine could end. Tokyo is looking to allow the Japanese industry ministry to help redirect LNG supplies in the event of an emergency. The production of natural gas was down 1.7% year/year. Damage to the Nord Stream gas pipeline from Russia to Europe was caused by powerful explosions, Danish police said on Tuesday. Spain will extend a cap on regulated gas price increases for households and small and medium-sized companies by a year until end-2023 to help them cope with soaring energy prices, Energy Minister Teresa Ribera said on Tuesday after a cabinet meeting. Member states are still in disagreement over what form the price cap should take. Europe prays for a mild winter and friends in far flung places – from the US freeport facility to private Chinese companies that may be able to increase LNG exports to Europe during the heating season. European countries and gas traders are reeling from the latest LNG supply shock - a force majeure from Nigeria LNG - that threatens nearly 4% of global supply and further squeezes the continent's resources in absence of Russian pipeline gas.

summary: Russia may have already begun hybrid warfare against Norway and northern Europe, especially Germany, to exploit Europe’s energy needs over the coming winter. US gas market balances are improving as supply strengthens and demand remains bearish. Shale oil and gas producer EOG Resources Inc paid $847 million during the third quarter to settle wrong-way bets on energy prices, the company said in a regulatory filing on Tuesday. The Russian operator of a pipeline that supplies Turkey and the Balkans with natural gas said it would suspend some maintenance and repair work, citing European Union sanctions, a move that threatens to deepen Europe’s energy crisis. The announced reduction in output has raised the temperature in Washington. Cooler heads are ultimately likely to prevail. Italy could face a gas shortfall of 5-6 billion cubic meters in the winter of 2023-24 without a new regasification terminal, the CEO of energy major Eni Claudio Descalzi said on Tuesday. Simultaneously, 26 offshore oil and gas blocks are also being offered in a separate round. The Spanish government will seek to reduce national natural gas consumption by at least 5.1% and potentially by as much as 13.5% in the period between August and March under a new energy contingency plan, the energy minister said in a presentation. Polish operator PERN has detected a leak in one pipeline in the Druzhba system that carries oil from Russia to Europe, it said on Wednesday. Germany and the Netherlands have proposed a package of 10 measures that the European Union could use to curb gas prices and avoid fuel rationing, including looking into setting a new benchmark price for liquefied natural gas. There are sufficient gas resources to support liquefaction options, the ministry said. Portugal will inject 3 billion euros ($2.91 billion) in its electricity and natural gas systems to curb energy prices paid by companies next year via a combination of state spending and regulatory measures, the government said on Wednesday. President Vladimir Putin said on Wednesday that Russia could redirect supplies intended for the damaged Nord Stream pipelines to the Black Sea to create a European gas hub in Turkey, or even use the one intact part of Nord Stream 2 to supply the EU. BASF is to reduce annual costs by 500 million euros ($485 million) in Europe up to 2024, including job cuts, as the German chemicals group took a 740 million euro writedown linked to the Nord Stream 1 pipeline. Israel's cabinet on Wednesday endorsed a U.S.-brokered deal to delineate a maritime border with Lebanon, paving the way for a potentially fractious two-week parliamentary review before it goes into force. Spain's BBVA has raised its sustainable finance target to 300 billion euros ($291 billion) for the period between 2018 and 2025 from a current goal of 200 billion euros, the lender's chairman, Carlos Torres, said on Wednesday. The OPEC+ ministers’ decision to institute a headline 2-million-barrel-per-day (mbpd) production cut among the cartel’s member states this week can only be interpreted through the lens of a wider, and ever-escalating, geopolitical crisis in Europe.
